case.paper_title: Human Capital and Development Accounting: New Evidence from Wage Gains at Migration
case.focal_claim: ... immigrants who have never been to high school gain ... more on migration to the United States than immigrants with a college degree (p. 682.)
case.hypothesis: Among immigrants in the authorized wage-gain data, the log wage gain from the last home-country job to the last U.S. job is larger for immigrants with no high school schooling than for immigrants with a college degree.

tasks_info.task_instruction: In Task 1, the analyst was asked to conduct the analysis without any restrictions.
tasks_info.task_goal: Test whether the focal claim is supported.

tasks_info.task_instruction: You should use the pooled sample of immigrants from poor countries in the NIS (New Immigrant Survey) and the Migration Projects, including Mexico. You should not control for sector: agriculture/nonagriculture, and region i.e. whether an immigrant grew up in a rural or an urban area.
tasks_info.task_goal: Produce one statistical result comparable to the original paper's focal result.

plan.path_summary: Estimate the no-high-school versus college-degree difference in log wage gains using OLS after prespecified trimming of the constructed log wage gain at the 1st and 99th percentiles. Task1 uses an unrestricted adjusted specification; Task2 uses the required pooled poor-country sample including Mexico with no controls.

path_signature.model_family: OLS linear regression with HC1 robust standard errors after 1%/99% trimming of constructed log wage gain
controls: Task1: country, sex, age_home_job, age_home_job_sq, yearLastHomeJob, yearLastUsJob
path_signature.sample_restriction: Use authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx rows with required variables, positive adjusted wages, and log_wage_gain within the 1st to 99th percentile range; Task2 retains Mexico and all countries in the authorized pooled file.
path_signature.missing_data_rule: Listwise deletion on required raw and constructed variables before trimming.
path_signature.variable_construction: Compute log_wage_gain = log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted). Categorize edyrs as no_high_school <= 8, some_high_school 9-11, high_school = 12, some_college 13-15, college_degree >= 16; college_degree is the reference group.
path_signature.inference_rule: A no_high_school coefficient greater than zero relative to college_degree supports the focal claim; p < 0.05 indicates strong statistical evidence and p >= 0.05 with a positive estimate indicates weak directional support. A negative estimate is inconclusive unless p < 0.05 and the confidence interval excludes zero in the negative direction, which is classified as opposite.

analysis_path.path_description: Use the authorized wage-gain table to regress trimmed individual log wage gain on education groups, estimating the no-high-school versus college-degree contrast while adjusting for country, sex, age at last home job, age squared, and last home/U.S. job years.
preprocessing_steps: Read data/wage_gain_table.xlsx.
Verify required columns: edyrs, yearLastHomeJob, yearLastUsJob, sex, yrborn, lastHomeWageAdjusted, lastUsWageAdjusted, country.
Drop rows missing required columns.
Require lastHomeWageAdjusted > 0 and lastUsWageAdjusted > 0.
Construct log_wage_gain as log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted).
Construct edu_group from edyrs: no_high_school <= 8, some_high_school 9-11, high_school 12, some_college 13-15, college_degree >= 16.
Construct age_home_job = yearLastHomeJob - yrborn and age_home_job_sq = age_home_job squared.
Drop rows missing constructed variables.
Compute the 1st and 99th percentiles of log_wage_gain and retain rows within those cutoffs.
Fit OLS regression with HC1 robust standard errors using college_degree as the education reference group.
Report sample flow, trimming cutoffs, education group counts, coefficient, p-value, 95% confidence interval, exponentiated percent difference, direction, conclusion class, and statistical strength.

models.formula: log_wage_gain ~ C(edu_group, Treatment(reference='college_degree')) + C(country) + C(sex) + age_home_job + age_home_job_sq + yearLastHomeJob + yearLastUsJob
models.planned_estimation: HC1-robust OLS coefficient for no_high_school relative to college_degree.
models.inference_criteria: The focal claim is directionally supported if the no_high_school coefficient is positive; statistical strength is strong if p < 0.05 and weak_directional otherwise. A negative coefficient is opposite only with affirmative statistical evidence against zero in the negative direction.
models.qualification: Task1 has no restrictions. Adjusting for verified demographic, country, and timing variables and trimming extreme constructed wage gains are defensible robustness choices for the same focal contrast; the paper summary notes outlier exclusions in sample construction, and the authorized dataset contains extreme adjusted wage values.

outcome.definition: Difference between log adjusted U.S. wage and log adjusted last home-country wage.
outcome.variable_construction: log(lastUsWageAdjusted) - log(lastHomeWageAdjusted), after requiring both adjusted wages to be positive.
outcome.missing_data_handling: Rows missing either wage or with nonpositive wages are removed before construction; rows with missing constructed log_wage_gain are removed.
outcome.qualification: The paper studies wage gains at migration using adjusted pre- and post-migration wages; log differences implement the wage-gain comparison.

main_predictor.name: edu_group
main_predictor.definition: Five-category schooling group based on years of education.
main_predictor.variable_construction: edyrs <= 8 is no_high_school; 9-11 is some_high_school; 12 is high_school; 13-15 is some_college; edyrs >= 16 is college_degree. college_degree is the reference group.
main_predictor.missing_data_handling: Rows with missing edyrs or uncategorizable education are removed.
main_predictor.qualification: The focal claim explicitly compares immigrants who have never been to high school with immigrants with a college degree; intermediate education groups are retained rather than restricting only to focal categories.

method_justification.claim_alignment: Both tasks estimate the same focal education contrast on the same wage-gain outcome: whether immigrants who have never been to high school gain more after migration to the United States than immigrants with a college degree.
method_justification.dataset_alignment: Both tasks use only the authorized data/wage_gain_table.xlsx file. Task2 treats this file as the authorized pooled poor-country NIS/Migration Projects sample and retains Mexico.
method_justification.method_reason: OLS on log wage gain provides a direct mean contrast in the outcome scale used for wage-gain comparisons. Education categories preserve the focal no-high-school and college-degree groups while retaining intermediate schooling groups. Symmetric 1%/99% trimming is a defensible robustness choice because the paper summary notes outlier exclusions and the inspected adjusted wage variables contain extreme values. Task1 uses unrestricted adjustment for verified demographic, origin, and timing variables; Task2 uses no controls to comply with the instruction.
method_justification.novelty_reason: Shared Memory path01 used untrimmed OLS models and path02 used untrimmed median quantile regressions. This path differs by applying a prespecified 1%/99% trimming rule to the constructed log wage gain while otherwise preserving the focal contrast and, for Task2, the no-control requirement.

self_check.self_check_note: The plan uses the same focal claim and authorized wage_gain_table.xlsx dataset. It writes separate Task1 and Task2 executable scripts. The path is distinct from prior shared-memory candidates because it uses OLS after prespecified trimming of the constructed log wage gain, rather than untrimmed OLS or median regression.

execution_directives.instructions: Execute Task1 and Task2 from the study root using the authorized original dataset and produce structured JSON outputs printed to stdout and written inside each candidate artifact directory.

debugging_rule.repair_scope: Fix dependency, file path, or output extraction issues only; do not redesign the analysis, change the focal claim, change variables, alter trimming, or add/remove controls.

execution_directives.comparison_metrics: For each task: no_high_school_vs_college_degree_log_wage_gain_coefficient, exp(coefficient)-1 percent difference, p-value, 95% confidence interval, final analytic sample size, direction, conclusion_class, and statistical_strength.
